text:
hana: FYI new canary (rerank-q4-int8) shows total NDCG ~flat but MRR -3% on the clinical holdout. Short queries (<6 tokens) and titles-with-unicode seem overrepresented in failures.

diego: Do we have the per-slice CSV? Want to check top1 vs top3 deltas and query_len buckets.

hana: Uploaded short summary + disagreements: s3://bench/rerank/3222339999/summary.csv and s3://bench/rerank/3222339999/disagree_examples.jsonl
```
model,cohort,ndcg,mrr,top1
float32,clinical-holdout,0.641,0.512,0.56
int8,clinical-holdout,0.639,0.497,0.49
```

pri: Two quick potential causes: tokenizer changes in quant build (unicode mapping) or last-linear scaling tweak. Did we change tokenization code in the quant commit?

diego: I recall a small normalization map for punctuation in the quant branch to stabilize embeddings. Could be it. If the token boundaries shift for e.g. greek letters or em-dashes, logits change.

hana: Ran a tokenizer parity diff on 5k queries. Result: ~0.8% tokens differ overall but concentrated on short-title samples. I dropped a sample: query "child asthma ") vs tokenized variants differ because of NBSP vs space variants.

atlas-bot: Perf-run 3222340010 finished. Logs: https://ci.redwood.prod/jobs/3222340010

pri: Can we do two fast ablations: (1) int8 but force tokenizer from float build, (2) int8 with float32 final linear copied (mixed-last). That isolates tokenization vs quantization math.\

hana: Kicked both off on a 15k subset: jobs 3222340055 (A), 3222340066 (B). ETA ~25m.

diego: Also add a small experiment: canonicalize whitespace/unicode before tokenization for clinical cohort (pre-token normalize) and rerun a cheap pass to see if flips reduce. If that helps, we probably should add a canonicalizer to the medical pipeline.

ops: Note for rollout playbook: add a check that eval harness uses identical tokenizers and normalization flags between float and canary runs. We had a near-miss last quarter. Ticket created: RERANK-5222.

hana: Early results: A (int8 + float-tokenizer) recovers ~1.6% MRR on short-query slice. B (mixed-last-layer) recovers ~0.9%. Canonicalize pass prototype recovers ~1.3%. So tokenization mismatch is primary, last-layer quant adds some extra jitter.

pri: Good data. Proposed actions: 1) revert the small tokenizer normalization difference in the quant branch, 2) add pre-token canonicalizer for clinical cohort, 3) keep mixed-last-layer fallback as low-risk mitigation.

diego: Agreed. Also add a dashboard micro-slice for "title-like-short-queries" and a CI diff that asserts tokenization-identical for canaries.

hana: Filing PRs now. Will re-run full canary after revert and canonicalizer add. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
